text:
[LFAC.2.6.4] `tolerance` is legal on **`logical`** schemas only.
It drives the no-op dedup above — a within-tolerance reassertion
of the same identity ([LFAC.1.7]) is suppressed — so it
presupposes identity dedup. A `ttl` / event fact carries no
identity markers ([LFAC.1.7.6]) and does not dedup; such facts
accumulate and expire on their deadline, so `tolerance` has
nothing to suppress there. `tolerance` on a `ttl`-scoped schema
is therefore a compile error (`DS_VALIDATE_TOLERANCE_TTL_SCHEMA`;
grammar rule [LGRA.5.9.5]). The rule is **`logical`-only**, not
merely `ttl`-specific: the compiler rejects `tolerance` on every
non-`logical` lifecycle (`ttl`, `explicit`, `ambient`), matching
the runtime, which rejects it on any non-`logical` schema at
load. The `ttl` case (the common one) reports
`DS_VALIDATE_TOLERANCE_TTL_SCHEMA`.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_fact
idris.note: The clause's premise only: identity dedup exists for the `logical` lifecycles and an explicit fact never dedups (every emit is a new fact), which is what makes `tolerance` meaningless there. `tolerance` itself is not modelled.
